sentences.text: During the third quarter of 2024, in connection with the planned sale of our seller financing loan portfolio, we performed a quantitative goodwill test and determined that the goodwill associated with Transaction banking and other was impaired, and accordingly, recorded a $14 million impairment.

(3) 2022 includes (i) an approximate $535 million (approximately $489 million after-tax) goodwill write-down due to resegmentation and the timing of Asia consumer banking business divestitures; (ii) an approximate $616 million gain on sale recorded in revenue (approximately $290 million after-tax) related to the Philippines consumer banking business sale; (iii) an approximate $209 million gain on sale recorded in revenue (approximately $115 million after-tax) related to the Thailand consumer banking business sale; and (iv) approximately $161 million (approximately $108 million after-tax) in operating expenses primarily related to separation costs in Mexico and severance costs in the Asia exit markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: A quantitative impairment test compares the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount including goodwill. If fair value is less than carrying amount, the impairment loss equals the excess, limited by the carrying amount of goodwill allocated to that unit.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS disclose performing a quantitative goodwill impairment test triggered by specific events or annual cycles. GS recorded a $14 million impairment in Q3 2024 in the Transaction banking and other segment due to the planned sale of its seller financing loan portfolio, indicating a quantitative test determined the carrying amount exceeded fair value. Similarly, MS defines the quantitative impairment test methodology as comparing the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount to determine if an impairment loss exists if fair value is less than carrying value, though MS does not report an impairment charge in this specific disclosure, stating instead that fair values were substantially in excess of carrying values.

sentences.text: During the third quarter of 2024, in connection with the planned sale of our seller financing loan portfolio, we performed a quantitative goodwill test and determined that the goodwill associated with Transaction banking and other was impaired, and accordingly, recorded a $14 million impairment.
When performing a quantitative impairment test, we compare the fair value of a reporting unit with its carrying amount, including goodwill.

If the fair value of the reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, the goodwill impairment loss is equal to the excess of the carrying value over the fair value, limited by the carrying amount of goodwill allocated to that reporting unit.
